claim_verdicts.suggested_text: Yes/no values read as questions, methods as verbs, collections as plurals; abbreviations and type prefixes make the reader decode, unless the short form is one the whole team already reads, like `Vnd`.

Consistent with identifier-names.md L38 "Prefer clarity over brevity." and general-naming-conventions.md L29 "DO favor readability over brevity."

identifier-names.md separates the two: L15 "Valid identifiers must follow these rules. The C# compiler produces an error for any identifier that doesn't follow these rules"; L29 conventions "provide consistency for names, but the compiler doesn't enforce them. You're free to use different conventions in your projects." The doc supports team consistency over a convention, not over 'any single naming rule'.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: When the team already has a word for a thing, keep it even if it breaks a shape convention; keeping that word matters more than any single naming convention.

issues.quote: consistency matters more than any single naming rule
issues.text: The pinned C# doc uses 'naming rules' for what the compiler enforces ('Valid identifiers must follow these rules. The C# compiler produces an error for any identifier that doesn't follow these rules') and 'conventions' for style ('the compiler doesn't enforce them. You're free to use different conventions in your projects'). Team consistency can outrank a convention, never a rule. The same wording appears in s5: 'keeping it matters more than any single rule'.
issues.fix: Summary line 4: change 'any single naming rule' to 'any single naming convention'. s5 last sentence: change 'keeping it matters more than any single rule' to 'keeping it matters more than any single naming convention'. Update claim 13 in .meta.json to the same wording.

issues.quote: a letter standing for a word, like `q` for quantity
issues.text: Definition too narrow: an abbreviation is any word cut short, not only a single letter. The lesson's own bad method name `Calc` (calculate) is a multi-letter abbreviation this definition does not cover, and quiz q4 option c treats `Tot` and `Ship` as abbreviations. The pinned guideline's example is multi-letter too: 'use `GetWindow` rather than `GetWin`' (general-naming-conventions.md L45).
issues.fix: Replace 'a letter standing for a word, like `q` for quantity' with 'a word cut short, like `q` for quantity or `Calc` for calculate'.

issues.quote: Abbreviations such as `q` and type prefixes such as `lst` make the reader decode first.
issues.text: Stated without the exception the pinned conventions make: 'Avoid using abbreviations or acronyms in names, except for widely known and accepted abbreviations.' (identifier-names.md L44). The lesson's recommended names end in `Vnd`, a short form it has to spell out for the reader two paragraphs later, so as written the rule contradicts the after-code. Summary line 2 repeats it unconditionally: 'abbreviations and type prefixes make the reader decode'.
issues.fix: In s4, after 'with `Vnd` for Vietnamese đồng', add: '`Vnd` is itself a short form; it is fine because everyone on the team already reads it.' In summary line 2 append ', unless the whole team already reads the short form'. Add that condition to claim 11 in .meta.json.
